title: Structured Output Gatekeeper: deterministic constrained-decoding for streamed tool invocations
creator: Asha Menon
description: Problem statement: When model responses are streamed while simultaneously invoking external tools, partial emits can violate the structured-output contract (malformed JSON, premature closing tokens, and interleaved toolcall tokens). This ticket implements a deterministic gatekeeper layer that enforces constrained-decoding during streaming and coordinates tool-call boundaries so that downstream decoders (constrained/lenient) always receive a well-formed, schema-adherent payload or a clear, machine-readable failure token.
background_and_rationale: We've observed a class of intermittent production failures where streaming partials from the generation path include tool-invocation markers or breakpoints that cause the constrained decoder to fail hard, cascading to 5xxs in the API. Existing tests exercise steady-state schema enforcement but do not reproduce timing/fragmentation patterns seen in dedicated and burst traffic. The gatekeeper will act as an intermediary: perform token-window validation, buffer minimal prefixes when necessary, and emit sentinel failure records (structured) when constraints cannot be satisfied within latency SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Under a synthetic streaming workload that interleaves tool calls 0-3 times per response, the gatekeeper guarantees either a schema-valid JSON object delivered to the constrained decoder or a standardized structured error (schema: {"message":"string","code":"string","phase":"string"}) within the configured latency SLO.

2) Existing constrained-decoding unit tests pass unchanged; new stress scenarios (fragmented prefixes, delayed tool-call acknowledgements, truncated KV cache) are added and pass deterministically in CI.

3) Canary traffic (mirror of 1% of production) shows no increase in API error-rate and demonstrates <5ms median additional latency for non-buffered responses and bounded tail latency for buffered cases.
4) Clear observability: per-request tag for gatekeeper_action {allowed, buffered, failed}, with histograms for buffer duration and token counts emitted.
5) Integration with rollout policies: canary flag and automatic fallback to legacy decoder path if gatekeeper OOMs or exceeds threshold errors.
6) Documentation: design doc + operator runbook checked in Confluence and linked in the PR description.

observability_notes: Instrument gatekeeper_action tag; emit buffer_ms and buffered_token_count. Wire alerts for: gatekeeper_error_rate > 0.5% 5m, median buffer_ms > 50ms for 10m. Ensure trace spans include gatekeeper decision and any buffer durations.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: buffering increases p95 latency and could cause timeouts upstream. Mitigation: conservative default mode = permissive-passthrough, enable guarded-buffer only in canary and for customers who opt in. Risk: OOM when many concurrent buffered responses; mitigation: bounded buffer per tenant and global eviction policy with structured failure emission.
release_notes_proposed: Add gatekeeper for structured outputs that reduces schema-related 5xxs during streamed tool interactions. Feature is behind canary flag; enable by default for runtime-1.20 after validation.
